judged_text: The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:9-15) is unauthenticated — it sends only calcomUserId + appSlug with no auth header, an inconsistent trust model given the inbound webhook requires a shared secret — and it has no timeout and its response status is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx/HTML error page is passed downstream as if it were a token payload.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no authentication headers and no timeout/abort signal. It also returns the raw `Response` without checking `response.ok` or validating content type/body, so callers will treat failures as usable responses. This is especially problematic because multiple call sites assume a successful token response shape (e.g., GoogleCalendarService reads `res?.data` after `refreshOAuthTokens`, which a `fetch` Response does not provide), meaning 4xx/5xx or HTML could propagate and/or break token refresh logic.
